What we treat

From annual skin exams to complex surgical care.

We see patients of every age, every skin type, and every concern — from the run-of-the-mill mole check to specialized Mohs surgery for skin cancer.

All services
M

Medical Dermatology

Acne, eczema, psoriasis, rosacea, hair loss, rashes you've been ignoring, and the annual skin exam you've been putting off. Everyday derm done well.

Conditions we treat
S

Surgical Dermatology

Mohs micrographic surgery for skin cancer, excisions, biopsies, and cyst removal — performed in-office with careful technique and thoughtful follow-up.

Surgical services
C

Cosmetic Dermatology

Botox, fillers, chemical peels, microneedling, and laser treatments. Elective and self-pay — but planned together with the same medical rigor as everything else.

Cosmetic options
P

Pediatric Dermatology

Kids get rashes, eczema, warts, and concerning birthmarks too. We see patients from infancy onward with kid-appropriate explanations and patient parents in mind.

Pediatric care
Our providers

A small team. You'll know who you're seeing.

Two physicians and a physician assistant — all with clinical privileges to spend the time your visit actually needs.

Full provider profiles
MD · FAAD · Medical Director

Dr. Ingrid Westgate

Founder and lead physician. General medical dermatology, complex inflammatory disease, and high-risk skin cancer surveillance. Fellowship-trained at Mayo Clinic.

Read full profile
MD · Mohs Surgeon

Dr. Marcus Tran-Whitfield

Fellowship-trained Mohs micrographic surgeon. Skin cancer treatment with same-day pathology and reconstruction. Also sees general derm patients on Tuesdays.

Read full profile
PA-C · Physician Assistant

Phoebe Aldarova

General dermatology with particular focus on acne management and pediatric derm. NCCPA-certified. Often the easiest provider to get in with for a quick follow-up.

Coming in for the first time?

We block 45 minutes for new-patient visits so we can take a full history, do a thorough exam, and actually answer your questions. Here's what helps your first visit go smoothly:

New-patient checklist & forms

45 minutes Time blocked for new-patient visits
5 forms Patient registration, history, HIPAA, insurance, photo release
Insurance card Bring physical card & photo ID
Medication list Including supplements & recent topicals

After-hours urgent concern?

For an existing patient with a clinically urgent dermatologic issue (suspected infection, surgical site concern, severe drug reaction), our answering service routes calls to the on-call provider.

(503) 555-1871
Life-threatening emergency?

Anaphylaxis, severe Stevens-Johnson reaction, uncontrolled bleeding, or any other emergency — call 911 or go directly to the nearest emergency department.

Call 911
